title: Hynish Archive

sources.title: Registration announced; original nine-member board
sources.summary: Report published 2 February 2023 says the AOA had been registered and lists an initial nine-member board. This is a publication date, not a verified registration date.

sources.title: Association website: registration number and board
sources.summary: Displays GBN/10037/2022-2023 and a board headed by Vinod Negi, labelled 2024-25. The live fetch returned an empty body; indexed content is not reliable proof of the present board. No original registration certificate was obtained.

sources.title: AOA notice: first GBM and handover roadmap
sources.summary: Notice dated 3 April calls a 7 April 2024 GBM. Agenda covers former-AOA/EC handover and a builder-services roadmap. Notice proves an agenda was issued, not that a transfer was completed.

sources.title: AOA notice: builder/GNIDA CAM handover and MOU
sources.summary: 17 July notice invites residents to a 21 July 2024 meeting about ongoing builder/GNIDA discussions, CAM handover, MOU and further action. The signed MOU and meeting minutes are absent.

sources.title: AOA notice: MOU compliance and NPCL multipoint
sources.summary: 14 December notice calls a 22 December 2024 GBM on infrastructure, NPCL multipoint and compliance with the Panchsheel Buildtech MOU. It establishes these issues were on the agenda by 2024.

sources.title: 1 August 2025 election judgment: 17915 with 19634
sources.summary: Common judgment quashed the 15 May 2025 Deputy Registrar order and remitted the matter to the Prescribed Authority. Judicial text was read; official signed PDF not obtained. Hindi quotation in the mirror is corrupted.

sources.title: 13 May 2026 judgment plus 20 May correction
sources.summary: Six-page court order sheet from the official High Court portal; includes the five-page decision and one-page date correction. Corrected dates are used in this archive. Neutral citation visible on the original: 2026:AHC:110600. Key PDF pages: 5 (directions), 6 (correction).

sources.title: Official case status: Writ-C 18764/2026
sources.summary: Captured 3 November 2026. Filed 7 May, registered 8 May; disposed 13 May. Correction IA filed 18 May and disposed 20 May. A stay IA still marked pending is a database field, not proof of operative relief.

sources.title: Official current case status: Writ-C 45508/2026
sources.summary: Filed 29 October; registered 3 November 2026. Pending, Newly Fresh. No first/next hearing date shown and portal says Order/Judgement Not Found. Full petition and interim prayers remain unavailable.

sources.title: Deputy Registrar reportedly halted proposed March election
sources.summary: 23 February 2026 reporting says a 1 March election was stopped while the earlier election dispute remained before SDM Dadri. It records residents challenging the proposed process. Original administrative order is missing.

sources.title: News interpretation of May High Court decision
sources.summary: 15 May report described elections within one month and quoted AOA assurances. The actual judgment has a two-stage timetable: reference decision first, election within one month thereafter. Use the judgment for the operative directions.

sources.title: 30 September SDM decision reported on 6 October
sources.summary: Reports dismissal for lack of sufficient one-quarter membership support and treatment of the 22 March 2025 election as valid. Article discusses 1,211 eligible voters, about 303 needed, and lists of 355, 174 and 85 signatures. It names the deciding officer as SDM Dadri Abhinendra Singh and says he directed the Deputy Registrar, Ghaziabad to take further action; no case number is given. Original order and lists are missing.

sources.title: October election-officer process reported
sources.summary: 17 October report says an officer nominated by Deputy Registrar issued directions on 15 October requiring AOA documents by 19 October. Also reports resident demands for financial transparency and facility improvements. Original notice is missing.

sources.title: Approved GH-08A site plan
sources.summary: Approved site plan for Plot GH-08A, Sector-1 (30,000 sq m / 7.41 acres), revised sanction stamped May 2014. Towers T1-T7 are stilt + 14 floors (84 flats each), T8 and T9 stilt + 24 (144 and 96 flats), T10 and T11 stilt + 20 (160 each), T12 stilt + 21 with community area (164). That is 988 flats at 2.75 FAR plus 324 purchasable-FAR flats = 1,312. It also records 1,132 car and 650 two-wheeler spaces (minimum 1,003 cars), projected population 5,904, ground coverage 31.27%, 10,326 sq m green area, a commercial block, three entries from service roads and 6 m fire-tender roads.

sources.title: Registered sublease exemplar: rights and handover clauses
sources.summary: A registered sublease publicly filed on UP RERA for one Phase-1 flat. Its schedule grants use of one covered car space; clause 30 says parking and certain facilities will not be handed to the association; clause 40 recognises applicable law. Not reproduced or linked here because it carries a buyer's personal details. Contract wording is not a ruling on enforceability.

sources.title: Allotment exemplar: FOC parking versus general clause
sources.summary: Allotment exemplar publicly filed on UP RERA. Page 3 itemises one covered parking FOC; page 9 clause 30 describes parking on request/payment, first-come-first-served and a separate agreement. Not reproduced here because it carries a buyer's personal details. Individual promises need reconciliation with boilerplate.

sources.title: GNIDA Tower-10 occupancy/completion certificate
sources.summary: Visually reviewed certificate dated 31 October 2018 concerns Tower-10, 160 units. Conditions include prior authority permission for changes and parking only in designated plan areas; it is not a whole-society occupancy certificate.

sources.title: January 2024 water crisis / builder-control context
sources.summary: 28 January report describes supply disruption, residents alleging builder water dues of about Rs 2 crore and an ad hoc AOA while builder remained in control. The maintenance representative disputed the dues and shortage account. No audited account or water-demand order was obtained.

sources.title: Water dispute, complaint and police intervention
sources.summary: 1 July 2024 reporting describes a resident assault complaint arising from a 23 June pump-room dispute, a police reconciliation meeting and warnings over hostile WhatsApp messages. This is not a conviction; original complaint, FIR status and police notice are not in hand.

sources.title: AOA response to criticism during water crisis
sources.summary: Reports Anjali Negi defending AOA response to June water problems, pump replacement/tankers and approaches to GNIDA/MP. It records supportive residents too. Publication date was not independently resolved; do not infer a judicial finding from the headline.

sources.title: Gate-2 boom-barrier disagreement
sources.summary: 27 August 2024 article describes gate access restrictions reversed after police intervention. Its title names Hynish but body says Panchsheel Heights; attribution needs corroboration. Its accusatory headline is not adopted.

sources.title: Water-quality notices in February 2025
sources.summary: Reports GNIDA notices to Hynish and Arihant Arden. The Rs 5 lakh fine described in the headline was imposed on Ecovillage-1, not Hynish. Hynish-specific notice and water-test results are missing.

sources.title: Basement-market flooding and maintenance concerns
sources.summary: 14 August 2025 report describes repeated basement-market flooding and trader losses at Hynish, with commercial area described as AOA-maintained. Loss amounts and responsibility were not established by an adjudication in the materials obtained.

sources.title: Shopkeeper complaint alleging duplicate maintenance charges
sources.summary: 19 August 2025 poster alleges maintenance deductions through a prepaid meter plus separate invoices. This website post is not a consumer-court judgment or verified case filing. AOA response and reconciled ledger were not obtained.

sources.title: Multipoint implementation dispute in late October
sources.summary: 2 November 2026 report says residents alleged obstruction when NPCL arrived after an asserted 22 October notice scheduling 28 October work. The actual NPCL notice, site report and AOA response are missing; obstruction and motive remain allegations.

sources.title: Cheque-dispute proceeding: Anjali Negi and two others
sources.summary: 21 April 2026 order in BNSS 8843/2026 concerns challenge to summons in Complaint 380/2025 (Panchsheel Buildtech v Panchsheel Hynish Apartment and others), Section 138 NI Act. It provides a compromise/compounding route and temporary protection; no acquittal, final settlement or parking relief is established.

sources.title: Tower-12 registry litigation: 29 owners
sources.summary: 9 April 2026 reporting describes a 90-day registry direction for 29 petitioning Tower-12 owners, funded by them. The case is Writ-C 13589/2026; as quoted by the Authority (S79) the order directed a decision on a representation, not registry. This is a separate ownership matter, not proof of an AOA election or parking outcome.

sources.title: UP Apartment Act 2010: statutory copy
sources.summary: Reference copy of the Act for framework and comparison. This archive does not certify that the copy includes every later amendment or decide the enforceability of a particular contract.

sources.title: Environmental recovery reporting includes Hynish
sources.summary: June 2026 report lists Hynish among societies in STP recovery action. The overall figures relate to 167 societies; no Hynish-specific liability amount, addressee or final recovery status was verified. Original demand/recovery certificate is required.

sources.title: Mid-2025 report: AOA declared time-expired; supply officer as election officer
sources.summary: Page metadata dates it 29 June 2025. Says the term ended 15 March 2025, the Deputy Registrar declared the AOA time-expired, the District Supply Officer was named election officer, and residents wrote to the DM for support and an ad hoc arrangement. No order date or reference is given. Fits the period after the 15 May 2025 DR order but is not confirmed by an original order.

sources.title: February 2026 complaint to DM about AOA functioning
sources.summary: 17 February 2026 report says the executive had not received formal Deputy Registrar recognition, the matter was before SDM Dadri, and residents alleged large collections for renovation and arbitrary GBM attempts. A resident sought an impartial DM inquiry. AOA office-bearers called all allegations baseless. No amounts or orders given.

sources.title: Late-October multipoint dispute: notice addressed to builder and AOA
sources.summary: 30 October 2026 report says NPCL had already surveyed the society, its 22 October notice went to both the builder and the AOA, and the 28 October team returned amid AOA opposition. Residents also allege single-point recharges were tied to other dues. AOA account not included; no UPERC direction or police record mentioned.

sources.title: NPCL post on Hynish multipoint consent (search-result lead)
sources.summary: Search-result text attributes to NPCL a post saying most Hynish respondents opted for multipoint, with an AOA-NPCL meeting on 20 May 2024 before a survey. The post itself could not be opened (X refused access), so wording, date and response counts are unverified.

sources.title: UPERC single-point to multipoint conversion framework
sources.summary: 2018 reporting on a UPERC suo motu Supply Code amendment directing conversion of single-point connections, with societies exempt only where 51% choose single-point. Later coverage (Outlook Business) records UPERC criticising discoms for delay. Coverage is 2018-2022; the current regulation text and any NPCL-specific order were not obtained.

sources.title: NGT groundwater case names Panchsheel Hynish as respondent
sources.summary: OA 392/2022, Prasoon Pant v Union of India: 5 July 2022 order lists Hynish among respondent builders accused of illegal groundwater extraction and directs a CPCB/UPPCB/DM joint committee report. No Hynish-specific finding or compensation appears in that order. Later UPPCB reports are hosted on greentribunal.gov.in but could not be opened (certificate error).

sources.title: GSTAT anti-profiteering order covering Hynish Tower-10
sources.kind: Legal news report of tribunal order
sources.summary: NAPA/59/PB/2025, DGAP v Panchsheel Buildtech, GSTAT Delhi, order reported as 20 February (2026). For Hynish Tower-10: 161 eligible buyers, Rs 29,68,382 profiteered. Builder to pass benefit with interest; 10% penalty if repayment delayed beyond 20 March 2026; compliance report within two months. Signed order and compliance not obtained.

sources.title: AOA formation reported, with president's statement
sources.summary: 3 February 2023 CitySpidey report (read via Wayback; live site unreachable). The first president said residents registered the association on 31 January 2023, renamed it Panchsheel Hynish Flat Owners Association, and that the nine members were chosen unanimously and announced at a general meeting.

sources.title: March 2024 election: two panels, 7-2 result
sources.summary: 21 March 2024 Tricity Today report (read via Wayback). Election held 16 March 2024 under an administration-appointed election officer; two panels contested, one won 7 of 9 seats. Office-bearers named: Anjali Negi (president), Amrendra Pratap Singh (vice-president), Vijay Rastogi (secretary), Himanshu Gautam (treasurer). Winners said getting handover from the builder was the main goal.

sources.title: AOA delegation meets the MP during water shortage
sources.summary: 26 June 2024. AOA office-bearers, a coordination committee and 40-50 residents met MP Dr Mahesh Sharma, who reportedly spoke to Authority officials and the builder and asked for a quick fix. The headline doubts follow-through.

sources.title: Memorandum demanding the 2025-26 election
sources.summary: 30 January 2025. Two AOA members handed the president a residents' memorandum asking for the 2025-26 election process and a GBM to form an election committee. No AOA response reported.

sources.title: Deputy Registrar cancels February 2025 GBM and committee
sources.summary: 8 March 2025. Report says residents complained the election committee formed at the 16 February 2025 GBM was one-sided; after hearing both sides on 28 February the Deputy Registrar cancelled that GBM and declared the committee invalid, so the planned 9 March election did not go ahead. Original order not obtained; no AOA response in the article.

sources.title: Deputy Registrar orders fresh election within a month
sources.summary: 18 May 2025. Reports a Deputy Registrar order for a fresh election within one month with the District Backward Class Welfare Officer as election officer, and that the time-expired AOA was limited to essential expenses. The account comes through a resident; a June 2025 report names a different officer (S33). The High Court quashed the 15 May 2025 DR order on 1 August 2025.

sources.title: DR stays proposed March 2026 election
sources.summary: 23 February 2026. After a complaint to the DM's office, the Deputy Registrar stayed the AOA election because the earlier election dispute was pending before SDM Dadri. Residents said the AOA announced a schedule unilaterally; the paper says the AOA president did not answer calls.

sources.title: Handover to AOA reported on 6 September 2024
sources.summary: Last updated 24 September 2024. Residents say the society was handed over to the AOA with the builder on 6 September 2024 without settling advance maintenance and IFMS, that maintenance rose 45%, and that the STP and pumps were not working. No AOA or builder response included; the handover document itself is not public. AOA records give 7 September 2024 (S89).

sources.title: AOA website noticeboard (archived snapshot)
sources.summary: 2 March 2026 Wayback snapshot of phaoa.in (live page returns empty). Shows GBN/10037/2022-2023, Plot GH-08A, office at T2-601, and notices for meetings on 12 March, 11 May, 13 July and 24 August 2025, plus a call for civil repair and painting proposals.

sources.title: Power-cut protests; NPCL cites damaged transformer
sources.summary: 27 May 2024. Residents protested long outages. NPCL said a transformer inside the society was damaged and that a notice had been served on the society.

sources.title: Water-queue video from Hynish draws coverage
sources.summary: 23 June 2024. A viral video showed residents queueing for water during the summer shortage.

sources.title: Residents protest over unopened swimming pool
sources.summary: 13 May 2024 (Apartment Times covered the same protest on 12 May). Residents said the pool was built about four years earlier but never started by the builder, and questioned maintenance spending. No builder response.

sources.title: Lift drop reported in Tower 3
sources.summary: 7 December 2024 roundup. Unnamed residents said a Tower-3 lift fell from the 3rd floor to the ground floor; the passenger was not injured. No date or official finding given.

sources.title: Basement market waterlogged after rain
sources.summary: 12 August 2025, spelled "Panchsheel Highness". Rain flooded the basement shops; management pumped water out; residents said it keeps recurring.

sources.title: Green-belt counters and fire-lane parking dispute
sources.summary: 26 October 2026, spelled "Highness" (matched by location and quoted resident; medium confidence). Residents objected to food counters in the market green belt and parking in the 6 m fire-tender lane; police calmed the situation; residents sought a joint district/GNIDA/fire inspection.

sources.title: Resident video: failed prepaid meter and disconnection threat
sources.summary: 2 November 2026, spelled "Highness". A resident says several prepaid meters failed within months, his was switched to temporary postpaid, and he was asked to buy a new meter rather than get a warranty replacement, with a disconnection threat; police attended. No AOA or NPCL response.

sources.title: Registry still pending a month after High Court order
sources.summary: 12 May 2026. About 300 families in two towers still awaited registry. Describes the 9 April order as directing the Authority to examine and decide within three months, and says residents reported no action by the Authority or builder.

sources.title: Tower-12 registry order: 29 petitioners, 90 days
sources.summary: 11 April 2026 Navbharat Times. Allahabad High Court directed completion of the sub-lease registry for 29 petitioning Tower-12 owners within 90 days; Tower 12 has 150+ owners and relief covers only petitioners. Describes the order differently from S56; the signed order is needed. The order as quoted by the Authority (S79) directed a decision within three months, not registry.

sources.title: UP RERA phase data (aggregator copy)
sources.summary: Phase 1 UPRERAPRJ8533 (T8-T9): start 8 Aug 2014, completion 8 May 2018. Phase 2 UPRERAPRJ8538 (T10-T11): 1 Oct 2015 to 1 Oct 2019. Phase 3 UPRERAPRJ8545 (T12): 2 Jul 2016 to 1 Jan 2021. All shown Completed on plot GH08A. The official up-rera.in portal could not be opened to confirm.

sources.title: Builder's project page
sources.summary: Status "Delivered", 12 towers, 1,305 units, RERA UPRERAPRJ8533, promoter UPRERAPRM6558. Gives no possession or certificate dates. Unit count differs from the approved plan (1,312).

sources.title: Property listing: phases and land area
sources.summary: Lists 12 towers, 1,312 units, 7.41 acres, Phase-1 launch 8 Aug 2014, Phase 2 Oct 2015, Phase 3 Jul 2016, and "ready to move since Jan 2021". Marketing listing; dates contradict each other in places.

sources.title: Property listing: plot, sizes and launch prices
sources.summary: Gives "Plot No. GH-08, Sector 1", launch Aug 2014, possession May 2018, 1,312 units, up to 24 floors, 7.41 acres, flats 755-1,550 sq ft, listed prices Rs 31.71-65.10 lakh (sold out). Marketing listing.

sources.title: Property listing: address and nearby places
sources.summary: Gives Sector 1, Bisrakh Jalalpur 201318, 12 towers, 1,312 units, 7.00 acres, possession January 2021; nearby Sarvottam International School (2.2 km), Noida Sector-101 metro (6.9 km), Gaur City Mall (7.1 km). Marketing listing.

sources.title: 2016 builder press release
sources.summary: 15 January 2016. Markets 2 and 3 BHK homes at a base price of Rs 3,724 per sq ft, with a 60 m front road, 24 m side road, club, gym and rainwater harvesting. Promotional text, not a verified record.

sources.title: 2019 snapshot: 700 families, 10 towers occupied
sources.summary: 30 August 2019. Says over 700 families lived in Hynish, with 10 towers occupied and 2 under construction. The rest concerns lift complaints.

sources.title: Supreme Court upholds Shahberi acquisition quashing
sources.summary: 6 July 2011. Supreme Court upheld quashing of about 156 ha acquisition in Shahberi, Greater Noida West, and fined the Authority Rs 10 lakh. Area-wide; Hynish not named.

sources.title: High Court quashes Patwari acquisition
sources.summary: July 2011. Allahabad High Court quashed acquisition of about 589 ha in Patwari and Dewla, where buyers had booked homes. Area-wide; Hynish not named.

sources.title: Builders allowed to resume after Master Plan 2021 approval
sources.summary: 28 August 2012. After NCR Planning Board approval of Master Plan 2021, the Authority let Noida Extension builders resume work after about ten months; the halt was treated as a zero period. Panchsheel not named.

sources.title: Supreme Court upholds Greater Noida acquisitions
sources.summary: May 2015. Supreme Court upheld the High Court approach of extra compensation (about 64%) and developed land for farmers; reported as removing the obstruction to construction. Area-wide.

sources.title: Greater Noida West metro link approved by PIB
sources.summary: 23 July 2026. Public Investment Board approved an 8.4 km elevated line from Noida Sector 61 to Greater Noida West Sector 4 (Gaur Chowk), about Rs 2,000 crore, pending Union Cabinet approval.

sources.title: NPCL multipoint progress across Greater Noida
sources.summary: 7 April 2026. NPCL says 91 societies now have individual connections (23 converted from single-point, 68 new); notices went to 130+ societies, some refused; UPERC order requires conversion. Hynish not named.

sources.title: UP Electricity Supply Code amendments index
sources.summary: UPPCL page (updated 20 November 2025) listing the 13th Amendment to the Supply Code 2005 on single-point and multipoint connections in multi-storey buildings and the UPERC order of 17 May 2019. The amendment text itself was not machine-readable.

sources.title: Commentary: AOA board term under UP Apartment Act
sources.summary: 10 January 2025. Explains the model bye-laws' one-year board term and their inconsistencies, and reports an Allahabad High Court ruling (Windsor Park RWA, Writ-C 12380/2023) that all board posts go to annual election. Secondary source, not the bye-law text.

sources.title: GNIDA allotment of the larger GH-08 plot
sources.summary: Greater Noida Authority letter No. Builders/2010/1414 dated 19 March 2010 allots Group Housing Plot GH-08, Sector-01 (204,000 sq m) to a consortium led by Supertech Ltd with Panchsheel Buildtech as a member, at Rs 10,044 per sq m, with premium payable in half-yearly instalments to 2018 and beyond. Read from the scanned copy filed with RERA.

sources.title: Lease deed for sub-plot GH-08A
sources.summary: Lease deed for Plot GH-08A, Sector-01 in favour of Panchsheel Buildtech, registered at Gautam Budh Nagar as document 17410 of 2010 (receipt dated 6 July 2010). Its endorsement records an agreement to lease executed 1 April 2010. Read from the scanned copy filed with RERA.

sources.title: GNIDA revised building-plan sanction for GH-08A
sources.summary: Letter dated 21 May 2014 grants revised sanction of the building plan on Plot GH-08A, Sector-01, valid five years, conditional on environment and groundwater NOCs. Conditions include gates opening only to the service road, no parking on the road, basement ventilation, and compliance with the UP Apartment Act 2010.

sources.title: "Hynish Specifications" sheet
sources.summary: Specification sheet signed 13 January 2018: earthquake-resistant RCC frame, vitrified-tile floors, granite kitchen platform, 2 or 3 high-speed lifts per tower, ISI copper wiring, intercom and DTH provision.

sources.title: Location: Google Maps listing
sources.summary: Google Maps lists "Panchsheel Hynish" at plus code HCHQ+J5, Sector 1, Bisrakh Jalalpur, Greater Noida 201318, near Supertech Ecovillage-1 and Nirala Greenshire Road (about 28.5791 N, 77.4379 E). Map pins are approximate.

sources.title: High Court judgment of 1 August 2025: official signed PDF
sources.kind: Primary court document · copy circulated to members
sources.summary: Digitally signed judgment (2025:AHC:129355, Court No. 32) in Writ-C 17915/2025 with 19634/2025; not a certified copy. Its Hindi passages are legible. It quotes the Deputy Registrar order of 15 May 2025, which discarded the 22 March 2025 election under Section 25(2) because the election committee was formed by show of hands and share certificates were issued selectively, barred policy decisions, and named the District Backward Class Welfare Officer as election officer. The Court found only procedural objections, which belong to the Prescribed Authority under Section 25(1), set the order aside and remitted the matter.

sources.title: Greater Noida Authority order of 15 July 2026 on the Tower-11/12 sub-lease representation
sources.summary: Order of the Authority's ACEO (Builders) under Allahabad High Court Writ-C 13589/2026, Sourabh Thukral and 28 others v. State of U.P. and 3 others. It quotes the High Court order of 9 April 2026: counsel confined the prayer to a decision on the home-buyers' 12 February 2026 representation, and the writ was disposed of without any view on the merits, the representation to be decided preferably within three months of the certified copy. After a hearing on 2 June 2026 the Authority records a part temporary occupancy certificate for 1,029 units/shops with 1,015 sub-leases executed, lease rent of Rs 92,97,055 due, and no completion certificate for Towers 11 and 12. It directs the builder to deposit the lease rent and, within three months, obtain completion for Towers 11 and 12 and execute sub-leases for their home-buyers. Letter number and day are handwritten. Not reproduced here because it names individual home-buyers.

sources.title: Deed of Declaration (Form A), 3 December 2015
sources.kind: Statutory declaration (scanned) · copy circulated to members
sources.summary: Form A declaration under the UP Apartment Act by Panchsheel Buildtech for "Plot No GH-08, Sector-1, 30,000 sq m", leasehold for 99 years under a lease deed of 6 July 2010. Annex B lists 12 towers and 1,312 apartments (84 each in T1-T7, then 144, 96, 160, 160 and 164). Annex D lists a single 7,513 sq m basement (STP, parking, ramp, panels, tank), lawns 875 sq m, play area 250, pool 213, basketball 428, two badminton courts, a 960 sq m club, and 2 lifts per tower in T1-T7 and 3 in T8-T12; it states "No parking provided in common area & Facilities" and gives the allotted area as 209,557 sq m, of which 30,000 sq m is Panchsheel's. Annexures E and F (limited common and independent areas), several original pages and any registration endorsement are not in this copy; area totals differ between clause FOURTH and Annex C.

sources.title: Authority meeting minutes no. 215 (27 May 2024)
sources.kind: Official minutes · copy circulated to members
sources.summary: Minutes of a 21 May 2024 meeting chaired by the Authority's ACEO (Builders) with the builder and AOA office-bearers. The society's electricity connection was still in the builder's name; the builder said it would transfer it if the AOA refunded the NPCL security deposit, and the AOA agreed. The AOA asked for multipoint supply. A draft handover agreement was being prepared, and handover of the connection and maintenance was directed by 15 July 2024.

sources.title: Authority minutes no. 234 of the 16 July 2024 meeting, with AOA letter of 18 July 2024
sources.summary: Minutes issued 25 July 2024 (day handwritten) of an Authority-builder-AOA meeting: the builder's MD said signing of the builder-AOA MOU was "in progress"; the AOA said MOU annexure points were unresolved; power, DG, STP, fire and lift issues were raised. The attached AOA letter of 18 July 2024 asked for a handover order before 1 August 2024 and cited an NPCL survey recommending three 1,500 kVA transformers. Not reproduced here because the attachment carries personal phone numbers and e-mail addresses.

sources.title: Deputy Registrar letter 3194 of 15 February 2025
sources.summary: Forwarding a residents' complaint of 11 February 2025, the Deputy Registrar told the AOA to hold its election under the UP Apartment Act 2010 and model bye-laws 2011. The complaint said the Deed of Declaration had not been amended; the letter quotes the joint-owner rule (only the first-named owner votes) and warns that an election against the rules would be void. Not reproduced here because its copy list carries residents' flat numbers.

sources.title: District Supply Officer (election officer) letter 638 of 1 July 2025
sources.kind: Official letter · copy circulated to members
sources.summary: The District Supply Officer, Gautam Buddh Nagar, nominated election officer by letter 600 of 20 June 2025, told the AOA to supply the Deed of Declaration, membership/voter list, registered bye-laws and an estimated election cost of Rs 2,56,000 by 5 July 2025 for an election within one month, warning of action under the UP Apartment Act 2010. Copied to the DM and the Deputy Registrar.

sources.title: Deputy Registrar order 3169 of 31 December 2025
sources.summary: Recalls DR letter 6021 of 25 August 2025, which referred the election dispute to the Prescribed Authority (SDM Dadri) under Section 25(1). On a complaint of 24 December 2025 that GBMs were being called while the reference was pending, it says that AGBMs not held according to the rules would be void. It does not itself declare particular meetings void. Not reproduced here because its copy list carries a resident's flat number.

sources.title: NPCL final notice of 17 July 2020 on multipoint
sources.kind: Utility notice · copy circulated to members
sources.summary: NPCL notice to the builder, the society and residents, after its letter of 21 August 2018 on the 13th Amendment to the Supply Code and reminders in 2020. Under the UPERC orders of 17 May 2019 and 2 March 2020, multipoint supply was presumed unless the association resolved by majority to keep single point; the society had 30 days or would be deemed to have opted for multipoint.

sources.title: NPCL notice 144 of 15 September 2026
sources.kind: Utility notice · copy circulated to members
sources.summary: Addressed to the builder's MD and the AOA President/Secretary, copied to UPERC, the ADM, the DCP and residents via the notice board. Requires compliance within 15 days with the UPERC tariff order of 10 October 2024 for single-point bulk consumers: half-yearly reports of amounts collected from residents against amounts paid to NPCL, and a CA audit uploaded to NPCL's portal. Penalties of Rs 5,000, 10,000 and 15,000 for the first three defaults; otherwise NPCL would begin withdrawing single point and converting to multipoint at the cost of "you / residents". One sentence is cut at the page break.

sources.title: NPCL final notice 156 of 22 October 2026
sources.kind: Utility notice · copy circulated to members
sources.summary: Addressed to the builder's MD and, by name, AOA President Vinod Negi and Secretary Vijay Rastogi; copied to the DM/ADM, DCP and UPERC. NPCL says that after seeking police help on 14 October, its team, police and service provider visited on 15 October 2026, met resistance from about 200 residents insisting on a fresh survey, and halted on police advice. It demands access within 24 hours and a nominated society representative, says the team will come again on 28 October, refuses a re-survey and warns of disconnection. Basis given: "three defaults" under the tariff order and the 13th Amendment, and resident complaints that electricity charges were adjusted into CAM and dues recovered through recharges. It does not say the AOA organised the opposition.

sources.title: AOA records giving the handover date
sources.kind: Association records circulated to members · seen, not reproduced
sources.summary: Three AOA minutes (22 December 2024, 24 August 2025, 17 February 2026) say the AOA took over maintenance from the builder on 7 September 2024; the AOA events deck and its annual "Hynish Day" on 7 September use the same date, and an AOA water circular gives "September 2024". The handover agreement and inventory themselves are not in these records. Not reproduced here because they are members-only minutes.

sources.title: Community: Hynish Day, cricket league and AOA events deck
sources.kind: Community notices circulated to members · seen, not reproduced
sources.summary: "Hynish Day" on 7 September marks the 2024 handover; a resident cricket league reached Season 4 in mid-2025 (52 players, 4 captains); an AOA deck shows festivals, national-day events, health and children's camps, plantation and cleanliness drives. Self-published by organisers: shows that events were held, not attendance. Not reproduced here because they carry residents' names and photographs.

timeline.title: Greater Noida Authority allots plot GH-08
timeline.body: Letter No. Builders/2010/1414 allots the 204,000 sq m Group Housing plot GH-08, Sector-01 to a Supertech-led consortium that includes Panchsheel Buildtech, at Rs 10,044 per sq m. Hynish later sits on sub-plot GH-08A.

timeline.title: Agreement to lease for sub-plot GH-08A
timeline.body: The registered lease deed for GH-08A records an agreement to lease executed on this date.

timeline.title: GH-08A lease deed registered to Panchsheel Buildtech
timeline.body: Registered at Gautam Budh Nagar as document 17410 of 2010. The approved plan later records the plot as 30,000 sq m (7.41 acres).

timeline.title: Land-acquisition crisis in Greater Noida West
timeline.body: The Supreme Court upheld quashing of the Shahberi acquisition, and in July the High Court quashed Patwari acquisitions; construction across Noida Extension was disrupted. Hynish is not named in these reports.

timeline.title: Builders allowed to resume work
timeline.body: After Master Plan 2021 approval the Authority let builders restart; the roughly ten-month halt was treated as a zero period.

timeline.title: Revised building plan sanctioned for GH-08A
timeline.body: Greater Noida Authority grants a five-year revised sanction. The approved site plan shows T1-T7 as already sanctioned and adds T8-T12.

timeline.title: Phase 1 (T8-T9) start date in RERA data
timeline.body: Aggregator copies of UP RERA data give 8 August 2014 as the Phase-1 start date (UPRERAPRJ8533). Listings use it as the launch date.

timeline.title: Phase 2 (T10-T11) start date in RERA data
timeline.body: UPRERAPRJ8538 covers T10 and T11.

timeline.title: Deed of Declaration lists 12 towers and 1,312 flats
timeline.body: Form A declaration under the UP Apartment Act. It lists the common facilities and says no parking is provided in common areas; the annexures on limited-common and independent areas are not in the circulated copy.

timeline.title: Builder press release markets 2 and 3 BHK homes
timeline.body: Paid release advertises a base price of Rs 3,724 per sq ft and lists a 60 m front road and 24 m side road.

timeline.title: Phase 3 (T12) start date in RERA data
timeline.body: UPRERAPRJ8545 covers T12.

timeline.title: Phase 1 completion date in RERA data
timeline.body: Listings give May 2018 as possession for the project; other listings say January 2021, the Phase-3 date.

timeline.title: Tower-10 completion certificate issued
timeline.body: Greater Noida Authority certificate for Tower-10 (160 flats), with conditions on parking only in designated areas.

timeline.title: About 700 families; 10 towers occupied
timeline.body: Hyperlocal reporting says 10 towers were occupied and 2 still under construction.

timeline.title: Phase 2 completion date in RERA data
NPCL final notice on multipoint consent
timeline.body: Under the 2019-2020 UPERC orders, multipoint was presumed unless the association resolved by majority to keep single point; the society was given 30 days.

timeline.title: Phase 3 (T12) completion date in RERA data
timeline.body: The last tower. Registry for many Tower-12 owners was still pending in 2026.

timeline.title: Registration-year identifier appears on AOA records
timeline.body: GBN/10037/2022-2023 appears on association notices and the AOA website. Exact registration day, certificate, memorandum and complete registered bye-laws are not public.

timeline.title: Residents register the association
timeline.body: The first president said the association was registered on this date and renamed Panchsheel Hynish Flat Owners Association.

timeline.title: Initial AOA registration and nine-member board reported
timeline.body: News names Diwakar Kumar president, Vishnu Srivastava vice-president, Anuj Kumar secretary, Anand Sharma treasurer; Sourabh Thukral, Ravindra Yadav, Bhaskar Kanungo, Brijendra Singh and Paresh Kumar members. Names transliterated from Hindi; not a verified current roster.

timeline.title: Water crisis while builder control was reported
timeline.body: Residents and an ad hoc-AOA member described water disruption and builder dues; maintenance disputed key claims. This does not establish the subsequent handover date or liability.

timeline.title: 2024 board election recorded in later judgment
timeline.body: August 2025 judgment records an admitted election on this date, with a one-year term through 15 March 2025. Primary result sheet and office-bearer transition records are not present. Contemporary reporting: two panels contested under an administration-appointed election officer; one won 7 of 9 seats; Anjali Negi became president.

timeline.title: First GBM notice: former-AOA, EC and builder handover
timeline.body: Letter PHAOA/24/1/033 called a 7 April meeting. It names Anjali Negi as president. Later records name Vinod Negi; original transition records are required rather than assuming these are interchangeable.

timeline.title: GBM scheduled on handover roadmap
timeline.body: The notice specified 7 pm at the badminton court. Attendance, resolutions and completion of handover have not been proved by this notice.

timeline.title: NPCL reportedly recorded majority multipoint preference
timeline.body: Search-result text attributes to NPCL a post on a majority multipoint response and a 20 May 2024 AOA-NPCL meeting before a survey. The post could not be opened; response counts and survey report are unverified.

timeline.title: Protest over unopened swimming pool
timeline.body: Residents said the pool built years earlier had never been started by the builder.

timeline.title: Power-cut protests; NPCL cites damaged transformer
timeline.body: NPCL said a transformer inside the society was damaged and a notice had been served on the society.

timeline.title: Authority minutes: connection still in builder's name
timeline.body: The builder would transfer the electricity connection if the AOA refunded the NPCL security deposit; the AOA agreed and asked for multipoint. A draft handover agreement was being prepared, and handover of the connection and maintenance was directed by 15 July 2024.

timeline.title: Managing body registration recorded by court
timeline.body: August 2025 judgment records registration of the managing body under Section 4(1). This is distinct from initial AOA registration. Original filed office-bearer list remains missing.

timeline.title: Pump-room confrontation described in later reporting
timeline.body: Reported assault complaint following unequal-water-supply concerns. No finding of guilt, FIR disposition or original complaint was verified.

timeline.title: AOA delegation meets MP over water shortage
timeline.body: AOA office-bearers and residents met MP Dr Mahesh Sharma, who reportedly spoke to officials and the builder.

timeline.title: Police reconciliation / WhatsApp warning reported
timeline.body: News describes a meeting of the parties and a police warning over inflammatory messages. Exact police record is absent.

timeline.title: Special meeting notice: CAM handover, MOU, action plan
timeline.body: Letter PHAOA/24/1/078 describes ongoing builder/GNIDA discussions and calls a 21 July meeting. It is not the signed MOU.

timeline.title: CAM-handover special meeting scheduled
timeline.body: Agenda included issues with builder, MOU discussion and resolution on the further handover plan. Meeting minutes and votes are missing.

timeline.title: Authority minutes: builder-AOA MOU "in progress"
timeline.body: Minutes of the 16 July meeting: the builder's MD said MOU signing was in progress; the AOA said annexure points were unresolved. The AOA then asked for a handover order before 1 August.

timeline.title: Gate-access dispute reported with society-name inconsistency
timeline.body: An article titled Hynish uses Panchsheel Heights in its body; treated as an attribution lead rather than a firmly matched Hynish incident.

timeline.title: AOA takes over maintenance from the builder
timeline.body: AOA minutes and its annual "Hynish Day" give 7 September 2024; one news report said 6 September. The electricity connection was not part of it: NPCL still billed the builder in 2026. The handover agreement and inventory are not in hand.

timeline.title: Lift drop reported in Tower 3
timeline.body: Residents said a lift fell from the 3rd floor to the ground; no injury reported.

timeline.title: GBM notice connects MOU compliance and NPCL multipoint
timeline.body: Calls 22 December GBM. It shows the multipoint and MOU-compliance agenda existed well before the October 2026 dispute.

timeline.title: GBM on MOU, infrastructure and NPCL scheduled
timeline.body: Actual minutes, MOU terms and follow-up decisions remain missing.

timeline.title: Residents' memorandum seeks 2025-26 election
timeline.body: Two AOA members delivered a memorandum asking for an election committee and GBM.

timeline.title: Hynish water-quality notice reported
timeline.body: News distinguishes Hynish notices from the Rs 5 lakh fine on Ecovillage-1. No Hynish fine is established by that headline.

timeline.title: Deputy Registrar: hold the election by the Act and bye-laws
timeline.body: Letter 3194 forwards a residents' complaint about voting rights and the unamended Deed of Declaration and warns that an election against the rules would be void.

timeline.title: General body process for next election recorded
timeline.body: Judgment recounts a process initially proposing elections for 9 March. Later administrative intervention changed the sequence.

timeline.title: Deputy Registrar cancels February GBM and committee (reported)
timeline.body: After hearing both sides, the DR reportedly declared the 16 February committee invalid. The High Court judgment separately records a 7 March DR direction.

timeline.title: Deputy Registrar directed fresh proceedings
timeline.body: Recounted in August judgment; original order absent.

timeline.title: Fresh notice for general body meeting
timeline.body: Issued following the 7 March direction, according to the judgment.

timeline.title: First meeting lacked quorum
timeline.body: Court recounts adjournment/fresh notice and a later meeting. Original attendance register not obtained.

timeline.title: Election committee constituted
timeline.body: Constitution of the committee and subsequent procedure became disputed. Allegations of procedural breaches are not automatically findings of fraud.

timeline.title: Election schedule declared
timeline.body: Election fixed for 22 March in the court-recounted chronology.

timeline.title: Disputed election held
timeline.body: Vinod Negi is identified as elected president in the August decision. Validity and handling of objections led to successive administrative and judicial proceedings.

timeline.title: Deputy Registrar discarded election, invoked Section 25(2)
timeline.body: Original order not obtained; its existence and treatment are recorded in the High Court judgment. The official judgment PDF reproduces the order: it named the District Backward Class Welfare Officer as election officer.

timeline.title: AOA reported time-expired; District Supply Officer as election officer
timeline.body: Report says the Deputy Registrar declared the AOA time-expired after the 15 March 2025 term end and named the District Supply Officer election officer; residents wrote to the DM. Order date and reference not given. The High Court quashed the 15 May 2025 DR order on 1 August 2025.

timeline.title: Election officer asks AOA for records and election cost
timeline.body: The District Supply Officer, nominated election officer on 20 June 2025, asked for the declaration, voter list, bye-laws and Rs 2.56 lakh by 5 July for an election within a month.

timeline.title: High Court quashed DR order and remanded
timeline.body: Writ-C 17915/2025 with 19634/2025 allowed; dispute returned to Prescribed Authority for fresh hearing, preferably within eight weeks from receipt of certified copy. This was not a final merits declaration validating every election step.

timeline.title: Basement-market flooding reported
timeline.body: Trader losses and maintenance concerns reported; engineering cause and legal liability not independently established.

timeline.title: Public complaint alleged duplicate maintenance billing
timeline.body: Forum post claims prepaid deductions alongside separate invoices. It is not a consumer commission order.

timeline.title: AOA notice for 24 August 2025 GBM
timeline.body: The AOA website listed notices for meetings on 12 March, 11 May, 13 July and 24 August 2025. Minutes are not public.

timeline.title: Deputy Registrar refers election dispute to SDM Dadri
timeline.body: DR letter 6021, recalled in the order of 31 December 2025, sent the dispute to the Prescribed Authority under Section 25(1) after the High Court remand.

timeline.title: Summoning order in builder cheque complaint
timeline.body: HC 8843/2026 later identifies an ACJM Ghaziabad summons in Complaint 380/2025. Complaint, cheque, amount, signatory record and eventual outcome are absent.

timeline.title: Certified-copy presentation / status quo in May narrative
timeline.body: May judgment paragraph 4 originally printed 19 October; correction order changes it to 9 October. Paragraph 5 also refers to a 9 October status-quo order. Underlying file/service records remain necessary.

timeline.title: Deputy Registrar order on meetings while the reference is pending
timeline.body: Order 3169: while the SDM reference is pending, AGBMs not held according to the rules would be void. It does not declare particular meetings void.

timeline.title: Restriction on policy / major financial decisions recounted
timeline.body: May paragraph 5 originally printed 27 February; 20 May correction changes this to 7 February. Scope, service and subsequent variation of original restraint are not independently established.

timeline.title: Residents seek DM inquiry into AOA decisions
timeline.body: Report says the executive lacked Deputy Registrar recognition while the matter was before SDM Dadri; residents alleged renovation collections and arbitrary GBMs. AOA called the allegations baseless. No amounts or orders given.

timeline.title: Status-quo / no-policy-decision order mentioned
timeline.body: April SDM extract reproduced in the May judgment mentions a 19 February order and an election-committee meeting. Alleged non-compliance was disputed; full administrative records are missing.

timeline.title: GSTAT anti-profiteering order covers Hynish Tower-10
timeline.body: Reported order in NAPA/59/PB/2025 computes Rs 29,68,382 for 161 Tower-10 buyers within a Rs 98.7 lakh total across three projects, with interest and a conditional 10% penalty. Separate from AOA, parking and election matters; compliance unverified.

timeline.title: Fresh elections notified
timeline.body: May paragraph 14 records this and the ensuing restraint. Notification itself is absent.

timeline.title: Election restraint recorded; proposed March poll stopped
timeline.body: May paragraph 14 identifies a 23 February order. Contemporary news describes a proposed 1 March election and resident objections.

timeline.title: Term expiry submitted to court
timeline.body: Petitioners argued expiry of the March 2025 committee term; the Court also considered Clause 26(iii) holdover pending successors. Term expiry alone does not describe the full legal position.

timeline.title: NPCL multipoint conversion across Greater Noida
timeline.body: NPCL reports 91 societies on individual connections and notices to 130+; UPERC order requires conversion.

timeline.title: High Court disposes of Tower-11/12 sub-lease writ
timeline.body: Writ-C 13589/2026 (Sourabh Thukral and 28 others) was disposed of without any view on the merits: the Authority was to decide the home-buyers' 12 February 2026 representation, preferably within three months of the certified copy. Early reports of a 90-day registry order overstated it. Text as quoted in the Authority's 15 July order; the signed High Court order is not in hand.

timeline.title: HC order on compromise route in cheque case
timeline.body: BNSS 8843/2026 disposed with conditional compromise procedure and limited no-coercive-measures period. It is separate from election litigation and does not establish final settlement.

timeline.title: SDM set aside March 2025 election
timeline.body: Operative SDM text is reproduced in May judgment. HC later rejected the reasoning; original complete SDM decision is missing.

timeline.title: Deputy Registrar consequential order
timeline.body: The May 2026 judgment discusses a Deputy Registrar action under Section 25(2) dated 29 April 2026, following the 24 April SDM order. The order itself is not public.

timeline.title: Writ-C 18764/2026 filed
timeline.body: Filing CIVIL12/112933/2026; diary 10863052026; registered 8 May. Parties include AOA and Vinod Negi against State, DR, Prescribed Authority/SDM and Anuj Kumar.

timeline.title: Registry still pending for about 300 families
timeline.body: A month after the April order, residents said neither the Authority nor the builder had started registry for two towers.

timeline.title: HC remanded reference question; set two-stage timetable
timeline.body: Order sets aside 24 April decision; considers why 25(2) rationale is inappropriate after restrained elections; directs reference-maintainability decision within one month of certified-copy production, then elections within one month of that decision. Read entire order.

timeline.title: Correction application filed
timeline.body: IA/2/2026 filed; disposal on 20 May is recorded in case history.

timeline.title: Three date corrections ordered
timeline.body: Paragraph 4: 19.10.2025 becomes 09.10.2025. Paragraph 5: 27.02.2026 becomes 07.02.2026. Paragraph 12: 22.03.2026 becomes 22.03.2025. Other apparent textual anomalies are not silently corrected.

timeline.title: Environmental recovery reporting: scope unresolved
timeline.body: Hynish listed in multi-society STP enforcement report; no Hynish-specific amount or AOA-versus-builder liability allocation verified.

timeline.title: Authority orders builder to complete T11/T12 sub-leases
timeline.body: Following the High Court direction, the Authority ordered the builder to deposit Rs 92,97,055 lease rent and, within three months, obtain completion for Towers 11 and 12 and execute sub-leases for their home-buyers. It recorded that completion had not been obtained.

timeline.title: Metro link to Greater Noida West approved by PIB
timeline.body: Proposed 8.4 km line to Gaur Chowk awaits Cabinet approval.

timeline.title: NPCL notice: collection reports and CA audit in 15 days
timeline.body: Addressed to the builder and the AOA under the 10 October 2024 tariff order; penalties for defaults, otherwise conversion to multipoint at "you / residents'" cost.

timeline.title: SDM reportedly dismissed election challenge
timeline.body: 6 October news reports insufficient one-quarter support. Obtain the signed decision before asserting its exact directions, signature findings or present effect.

timeline.title: Election-officer directions reportedly issued
timeline.body: 17 October report says required AOA records were due by 19 October. Original directions, election programme and compliance record remain missing.

timeline.title: NPCL visit halted after resident opposition
timeline.body: NPCL's account: about 200 residents opposed the conversion and asked for a fresh survey; police advised a halt. The notice does not attribute the opposition to the AOA.

timeline.title: NPCL final notice to builder and AOA
timeline.body: Notice 156 to the builder's MD and the AOA President and Secretary: access within 24 hours, a nominated representative, the team to return on 28 October, re-survey refused, disconnection warned. Its basis is "three defaults" under the tariff order, not owner consent.

timeline.title: Green-belt counters and fire-lane parking dispute
timeline.body: Residents objected to counters in the market green belt and parking in the 6 m fire lane; they sought a joint inspection.

timeline.title: NPCL installation reportedly did not proceed
timeline.body: Residents alleged opposition from AOA/supporters and team departure. This is not an independently verified finding of obstruction or motive. No record of what happened that day is in hand; NPCL's notice documents opposition at the 15 October visit.

timeline.title: Current Writ-C 45508/2026 filed
timeline.body: CIVIL12/276142/2026, diary 266021102026. Full petition/prayer pages have not been obtained.

timeline.title: Resident reports failed prepaid meter and disconnection threat
timeline.body: A resident says his prepaid meter failed within months, he was asked to buy a new one instead of a warranty replacement, and was threatened with disconnection; police attended. No AOA or NPCL response reported. A meter fault and the authority to disconnect are separate questions.

timeline.title: Current writ registered, pending; no order displayed
timeline.body: Writ-C 45508/2026; CNR UPHC056633602026. Stage Newly Fresh, no hearing dates displayed; Order/Judgement Not Found at capture. Portal silence is not a certified finding that no order exists anywhere.

cases.title: 2025 election challenge and High Court remand
cases.parties: PHAOA and Vinod Negi; connected petition by Sandeep Sharma and 17 others v State of UP and others
cases.forum: Allahabad High Court / Deputy Registrar / Prescribed Authority
cases.summary: Challenge to the DR decision discarding the 22 March 2025 election. On 1 August the High Court quashed the DR order and remitted for fresh determination.
cases.prayers: Judgment reproduces two main prayers: quash DR order dated 15 May 2025; direct DR to recognise the 22 March 2025 election. This is the 2025 writ, not the current 2026 petition.
cases.outcome: DR order set aside; both writs allowed with remand and hearing of both sides, preferably eight weeks from receiving certified copy. It does not finally resolve all electoral objections.
cases.missing: Full petitions/annexures, DR orders, result/attendance records, certified-copy receipt trail.

cases.title: 2026 SDM decision, High Court order and correction
cases.parties: PHAOA and Vinod Negi v State, Deputy Registrar, Prescribed Authority/SDM and Anuj Kumar
cases.summary: Challenge to April 2026 action. On 13 May the HC set aside the 24 April SDM order and directed a fresh reference-maintainability decision; it addressed the election restraint, bye-laws and a consequential DR order. The dispute reached SDM Dadri through DR letter 6021 of 25 August 2025 under Section 25(1).
cases.prayers: Full petition unavailable. Judgment identifies challenges to 24 April and 29 April orders; do not present reconstructed requests as the complete filed prayer clause.
cases.outcome: One month for reference decision from production of certified copy, followed by elections within one month of that decision. 20 May correction fixes three dates. September dismissal is news-reported; original unavailable.
cases.missing: April SDM/DR orders in full; complete petition, stay application, certified-copy production, September decision and October officer directions.

cases.title: Builder cheque complaint and quashing application
cases.parties: Smt Anjali Negi and two others v State and another; underlying Panchsheel Buildtech v Panchsheel Hynish Apartment and others
cases.forum: ACJM Court 3, Ghaziabad / Allahabad High Court
cases.summary: Section 138 NI Act summons dated 27 August 2025 challenged. HC order records a monetary dispute and possibility of compromise.
cases.prayers: HC application sought quashing of summons and entire underlying proceeding. This is stated in the order; full application and complaint unavailable.
cases.outcome: Disposed with a conditional route to seek compounding, deposit 10% of cheque amount and time-limited protection. Cheque amount, later payment, settlement or trial outcome unverified.
cases.missing: All accused names, cheque/amount/signatory, complaint, summons, settlement application and post-April order sheets. No inference that election/parking merits were decided.

cases.title: Tower-11/12 sub-lease registry case
cases.parties: Sourabh Thukral and 28 others v. State of U.P. and 3 others (cause title as quoted)
cases.forum: Allahabad High Court; Greater Noida Authority
cases.summary: Home-buyers sought sub-lease execution and a decision on their 12 February 2026 representation. The High Court disposed of the writ on 9 April 2026 without a view on the merits, asking the Authority to decide within three months of the certified copy. On 15 July 2026 the Authority directed the builder to pay lease rent and, within three months, obtain completion for Towers 11 and 12 and execute sub-leases for their home-buyers generally.
cases.prayers: As quoted in the Authority's order: sub-lease execution within a fixed time, and a decision on the 12 February 2026 representation. Counsel confined the prayer to the second.
cases.outcome: A direction to decide, not a registry order. The three-month registry window comes from the Authority's order and depends on a completion certificate that had not been issued. In May 2026 residents said registry had not started.
cases.missing: Signed High Court order with neutral citation; the petition; proof of completion and sub-lease execution after October 2026.

cases.title: Current election-control challenge
cases.parties: Panchsheel Hynish Apartment Owners and Another; Vinod Negi v State, Deputy Registrar Firm, Election Officer and Anuj Kumar
cases.summary: Filed 29 October; registered 3 November. CNR UPHC056633602026, filing CIVIL12/276142/2026, diary 266021102026. Official record confirms institution and parties.
cases.prayers: NOT OBTAINED. Descriptions of what this petition seeks, circulating among residents, remain unverified until the filed petition is seen.
cases.outcome: No first/next hearing date shown, and no order available in the captured public status. An operative stay has not been verified.
cases.missing: Complete filed petition with prayers, interim application, current authorising resolution and costs, any order since filing, current listing.

findings.title: The May deadline was repeatedly oversimplified
findings.body: The operative paragraph 16 has two stages: Prescribed Authority decides within one month of certified-copy production; elections follow within one month of that decision. It is not a standalone deadline of 13 June. Actual service and September decision are necessary to evaluate delay. If the reported 30 September decision is confirmed and paragraph 16 applies without modification, 30 October is a date to examine, not an independently established breach.

findings.title: Three corrected dates materially affect the chronology
findings.body: 20 May correction changes 19 October to 9 October 2025; 27 February to 7 February 2026; and 22 March 2026 to 22 March 2025. Original five-page versions and press reports can carry the old dates. The combined order is the better working reference. Paragraph 10 also prints 17195 rather than 17915; the correction order does not address this, so it is flagged rather than silently changed.

findings.title: Some delays predate the current writ
findings.body: The High Court itself records that elections notified on 21 February 2026 were stopped by an order of 23 February. That weakens any claim that every delay arose solely from AOA refusing to hold an election. It does not settle whether the October challenge was necessary, proportionate or resident-approved.

findings.title: No public account of AOA legal spending
findings.body: Residents publicly demanded accounts in October 2026 and alleged large collections in February 2026; the AOA called the allegations baseless and earlier defended its handling of the water crisis. No audited accounts or case-wise legal-expense statement is public, so neither the allegations nor the rebuttal can be checked from public material.

findings.title: Why 2024 notices and later records name different presidents
findings.body: Reporting on the 16 March 2024 election names Anjali Negi as president, matching the 2024 notices. The High Court judgment identifies Vinod Negi as president elected on 22 March 2025, matching later records. These are two different election results, not an inconsistency. Original result sheets are still not public.

findings.title: A parking-right promise survives a zero-price label
findings.body: One allotment exemplar itemises covered parking-1 as FOC, while its general clause 30 describes paid, first-come parking and a separate agreement. The separate sublease exemplar grants use of one covered parking in its schedule. These show specific promises need examination even where a separate parking price is zero. They do not establish that every flat has identical terms or decide enforceability.

findings.title: The sublease expressly attempts to exclude parking from handover
findings.body: Clause 30 says common services transfer to the association while parking and certain other facilities will not. The same deed contains a specific one-covered-space usage right and a clause requiring compliance with the Apartment Act/rules. This could help explain a services-versus-parking handover split, but it does not prove the clause is legally effective or the actual MOU adopted it. Obtain the signed MOU, declaration and parking inventory.

findings.title: The 180-space gap is not the same as a 180-space regulatory deficit
findings.body: The drawing records 1,312 homes and 1,132 proposed car spaces, a difference of 180. But it records minimum required car spaces as 1,003, so proposed inventory is 129 above that drawing minimum. These are different comparisons. Actual usable bays, approved later revisions and the total contractual promises still need audit. The sheet alone neither proves compliance today nor identifies owners without rights.

findings.title: Multiple phase filenames are duplicate copies, not separate corroboration
findings.body: Plan files filed under phases 1, 2 and 3 share one SHA-256 hash, and the sanction letter, land allotment and lease deed also appear under more than one phase. The common plan is whole-site in content. Repetition is not independent corroboration; a byte-level duplicate report is included.

findings.title: Tower numbers differ between sales and sanction records
findings.body: The sublease identifies a sanctioned Tower-9 with sales-plan Tower-7. Parking/right audits should match plot, sanctioned tower, sales tower and flat identifier before declaring mismatches. A similarly named Phase-3 document cannot be assumed to prove a current Tower-12 fact without mapping.

findings.title: Road and designated-use restrictions are explicit
findings.body: The Tower-10 certificate says no parking on road and use only as designated in the plan; changes require authority permission. The plan shows six-metre fire-tender roads and green areas. These documents justify checking actual occupation against approved geometry, not treating circulation/green space as spare permanent bays. The certificate covers Tower-10, not all towers.

findings.title: MOU and multipoint issues were already on the 2024 agenda
findings.body: July notice discusses CAM handover/MOU; December notice discusses MOU compliance and NPCL multipoint. Notices demonstrate acknowledgement and planned discussion, not completion, agreement terms, performance or legal fault. They provide a concrete document trail for requesting minutes, MOU annexures and implementation correspondence.

findings.title: Separate proceedings must not be used as substitutes
findings.body: The cheque matter, election writs, reported parking case and Tower-12 registry case concern different relief and parties. An order mentioning an AOA does not necessarily settle its election or accounts. Searches also surfaced unrelated cases where Hynish was only an address; those are excluded.

findings.title: Insufficient support is not the same as forgery
findings.body: Public reporting of the 30 September 2026 SDM decision says the challengers did not show support from one quarter of 1,211 eligible members. That is a finding about support, not a public finding that any signature was forged. Any forgery claim needs the order, the lists and a judicial or forensic finding.

findings.title: Meter replacement and disconnection are separate questions
findings.body: A meter may need replacing while the authority, notice and process for disconnection remain separate questions. The public resident account does not establish a cause of failure, who pays, or the legal basis for disconnection; no AOA or NPCL response is public. The wider multipoint conversion would change who supplies and bills each flat.

findings.title: Hynish sits on a sub-plot of a much larger 2010 allotment
findings.body: In March 2010 the Authority allotted the 204,000 sq m GH-08 plot to a Supertech-led consortium that included Panchsheel. Hynish is on GH-08A, a 30,000 sq m sub-plot leased to Panchsheel Buildtech in 2010. The sub-division record itself is not public.

findings.title: The towers were built in four stages
findings.body: The 2014 revised plan shows T1-T7 (stilt + 14) as already sanctioned and adds T8-T9 (stilt + 24), T10-T11 (stilt + 20) and T12 (stilt + 21). RERA data dates the three registered phases from 2014 to 2021, and a 2019 report had 10 towers occupied. Completion certificates for towers other than T10 are not public.

findings.title: Public numbers about the society conflict
findings.body: Unit totals: 1,312 (approved plan, most listings), 1,305 (builder website), 1,314 (one listing). Land: 7.41 acres / 30,000 sq m (plan) versus 7.00 acres (one listing). Plot: GH-08A (lease, plan, AOA website) versus GH-08 (a listing). Possession: May 2018 or January 2021 depending on the phase. The approved plan and registered lease are the stronger records. Allotted area of GH-08: 204,000 sq m (allotment letter) versus 209,557 sq m (Deed of Declaration).

findings.title: Two election officers in 2025, at different times
findings.body: Both reports fit the record. The 15 May 2025 DR order, reproduced in the official judgment, named the District Backward Class Welfare Officer. By 20 June 2025 the District Supply Officer had been nominated, and wrote to the AOA on 1 July asking for records and Rs 2.56 lakh. The High Court quashed the 15 May order on 1 August 2025.

findings.title: Public coverage is mostly complaints
findings.body: Almost all public news about Hynish carries residents' complaints. AOA statements appear in only a few items, and no public coverage of festivals or community events was found, though notices circulated to members show an annual "Hynish Day" on 7 September and a resident cricket league. The archive therefore says less about everyday community life than about disputes; that is a gap in public records, not a finding about the society.

findings.title: Handover: 7 September 2024 by AOA records, without the electricity connection
findings.body: AOA records give 7 September 2024; one news report said 6 September. Authority minutes show handover was directed by 15 July 2024, the electricity connection was still in the builder's name, and the MOU was "in progress". NPCL's 2026 notices are still addressed first to the builder. The signed MOU and inventory are not public.

findings.title: The Tower-12 order was a direction to decide, not a registry order
findings.body: The High Court's 9 April 2026 order, quoted in the Authority's 15 July order, asked the Authority to decide a representation within three months and expressed no view on the merits. Reports of "registry within 90 days" overstated it. The registry deadline is the Authority's own direction to the builder, depends on a T11/T12 completion certificate not yet issued, and covers Tower-11 and 12 home-buyers generally, not only the 29 petitioners.

findings.title: NPCL's 2026 case for conversion rests on defaults, not consent
findings.body: The 2020 notice used the consent route: multipoint unless a majority kept single point. The 2026 notices invoke "three defaults" under the 10 October 2024 tariff order (collection reports and a CA audit) and treat conversion as mandatory. Both 2026 notices are addressed to the builder, which still held the connection, and the AOA jointly; the notices do not establish which party defaulted, and the default letters themselves are not in hand.

findings.title: The declaration does not list parking as a common area
findings.body: The 2015 Deed of Declaration says no parking is provided in common areas, although its basement description includes parking. The annexures that would define limited-common or independent areas, where parking may have been placed, are not in the circulated copy. On this document the approved plan's 1,132 car spaces are not general common property; whether a reservation was lawful needs the missing annexures and the approved parking map.

chapters.title: The land
chapters.body: In March 2010 the Greater Noida Authority allotted a 204,000 sq m group-housing plot, GH-08 in Sector-1, to a consortium led by Supertech with Panchsheel Buildtech as a member. A 30,000 sq m sub-plot, GH-08A, was leased to Panchsheel the same year. Within a year, court rulings on land acquisition in Greater Noida West halted building across the area until 2012.

chapters.title: Building twelve towers
chapters.body: A revised plan approved in May 2014 kept seven towers of stilt + 14 floors (T1-T7) and added five taller ones: T8-T9 at stilt + 24, T10-T11 at stilt + 20 and T12 at stilt + 21, for 1,312 homes. The later towers were registered with UP RERA in three phases. Tower-10 received its completion certificate in October 2018; by 2019 ten towers were occupied, and the last phase was recorded complete in January 2021.

chapters.title: Residents organise
chapters.body: Residents registered an apartment owners' association, reported in February 2023 with a nine-member board under registration GBN/10037/2022-2023. In March 2024 an election under an administration-appointed officer chose a new board, which said its first goal was taking over the society from the builder.

chapters.title: Handover and everyday services
chapters.body: Through 2024 the AOA held meetings on handover, an MOU with the builder and NPCL multipoint electricity. In May the Authority directed the builder to hand over maintenance and the electricity connection by 15 July; in July the MOU was still "in progress". The AOA took over maintenance on 7 September 2024, by its own records, but the electricity connection stayed in the builder's name. The same year saw water shortages, power-cut protests and complaints about lifts, the pool and maintenance charges, with the AOA, the MP and authorities approached.

chapters.title: Elections in dispute
chapters.body: The board elected in March 2025 was challenged. Deputy Registrar orders, SDM decisions and two High Court judgments followed, with the courts sending questions back to the administrators. In September 2026 the SDM reportedly upheld the 2025 election; a new petition was registered in the High Court in November 2026 and was pending.

chapters.title: Where things stand
chapters.body: Open questions in late 2026 include the AOA election process; NPCL's mandatory multipoint conversion, which its October notice says about 200 residents opposed; registry for Tower-11 and 12 owners, where the Authority gave the builder until about October 2026 to obtain completion and execute sub-leases; a tax-tribunal order on passing benefits to Tower-10 buyers; and resident demands for public accounts. Each is tracked here with what the public record shows and what it does not.
